title: Present independently authorized Investigate Case chronology as bounded human-readable HTML after Command Incident navigation
goal: Complete the already-working same-origin Command Incident linked-Case navigation by rendering source-authorized CAP-INV-110 Timeline entries, provenance and correction states as an accessible HTML view rather than raw JSON; preserve every JSON client's contract and independent source ownership.
invariants: Only existing GET /case-timeline is used, no new trusted SessionResolver or provider, permission, read/write operation, or destination route.
HTML rendering occurs AFTER the full independent Investigate Case, Timeline Entry and typed-source authorization for exactly the same Result consumed by JSON clients.
Command Incident and Shared linked-Case navigation alone NEVER authorizes Investigate Case; HTTP errors remain generic and contain no forbidden Case/Entry/source metadata.
Browser Accept text/html gets strictly <=200 visible entries; default HTML page <=50; JSON clients retain original unpaged/paged wire bytes.
Only owner-authorized source fields and superseded boolean are text-escaped by Go html/template, never injected into unsafe JS or marked verified observation.

Unknown/missing successor flag is NOT presented as current; corrected predecessor and successor remain distinct across pages; next-page links preserve only previously syntactically validated Case/query selectors.
Browser navigation to Work Queue is an optional re-authorized destination, NOT restoration of exact Incident selection; OPEN-013 Class-2 mutations excluded.
Current base #199 exact SHA remains immutable for existing independent L2 and old command/investigate/case rights remain separate.
security_properties: No HTML is rendered for denied, invalid, anonymous, cross-environment, or foreign Case, even if Command link is visible.
Content Security Policy default-src none, no scripts, referrer-policy no-referrer, X-Frame-Options DENY, no-store and nosniff on authorized HTML.
Source, timestamps, provenance, source ref, Case selector, pagination links are escaped and never raw HTML; scripts are not executed.
No hidden/off-page entries are rendered; counts refer only to authorized, filtered entries; paging never assumes transactionally stable event set.
Accept application/json or absent keeps existing JSON semantics, including JSON errors for malformed/denied requests.

migration.rationale: A bounded HTML representation of an existing read-only authorized JSON endpoint. No persistent schema, owner, or API route changes.

rollback.strategy: Remove case_html.go and content negotiation branch; existing JSON and source-authorized navigation remain unchanged.
verification: Original JSON with absent/explicit JSON Accept identical
Command/Investigate endpoints preserve authorization and status codes

inputs: CAP-CMD-106 and CAP-INV-110 navigation/read-only canonical transitions with independently authorized linked Cases.
PR #199 source SHA 18826ea501f040768c24dbc9b742000af0da8abd already composed two real Go HTTP handlers with separate synthetic IAM owner fixtures.
Existing CAP-INV-110 Project and CaseTimelineHTTPHandler returns authorized source/provenance and superseded status in JSON.
outputs: Human-readable read-only Timeline page for browser Accept text/html with owner-authorized old/new version status, source provenance, time uncertainty and accessible pager.
Existing selected Incident links now navigate into a useful Case screen rather than raw JSON, under the same host; no new case entitlement.
Exact-HEAD Go root and cross-product host tests including browser Accept, HTML escape, forbidden source redaction, denied Command-only viewer, and JSON compatibility.
acceptance_tests: Existing Work Queue selected Incident HTML link opens real GET /case-timeline Accept text/html and displays only its separately authorized Case timeline.
HTML first page shows old event superseded even when newer authorized successor on another page; next page includes authorized new version and original Supersedes.
Command-only principal, anonymous, bad session and foreign Case cannot receive HTML or protected event/source references.
Source-controlled HTML/JS tokens escape under html/template, content security headers are present, no inline scripts or unsupported source action invented.
Absent or application/json Accept yields source-identical existing JSON response.
Filters/paging preserve a validated selection and do not leak excluded or denied Case data; HTML default limited to 50 entries and explicit limit max 200.
Linux/macOS/Windows Go tests, Linux race, Go vet, exact-head engineering kernel security/architecture/complexity and source E2E gates all succeed without waiver.
definition_of_ready: E10-CMD-106F-TIMELINE implemented and CI green on exact #199 source; existing Go handlers compose independently and source-visible Timeline corrections supplied.
Read-only HTML response needs no OPEN-013 mutation or a new canonical product decision.
No frozen parent PR is edited; all work belongs to the new child branch.
definition_of_done: Actual linked Incident to authorized human Timeline HTML can be exercised across the same Go host with source-negative tests.
Both timeline and cross-product host CI green on exact HEAD and required security/engineering gates pass.
L2 material cross-product browser/data exposure review distinct from author; merge blocked until parent and approver conditions.
No production identity provider, deployed browser, durable Case data or native approval asserted.

performance_budget.rationale: At most 200 HTML-rendered entries per request, with existing source-bound 5000-entry Project, no new provider calls; synthetic performance only, no production SLO.
